newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LG Group in Vietnam rare earth venture.
newsitem.headline: LG Group in Vietnam rare earth venture.

text.p: South Korea's LG Group has entered into a US$12.7 million contract to develop a rare earth mine in Vietnam, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.

It said the proposed development was a joint venture with a subsidy of the Vietnam National Minerals Corp (VNMC) and the Korea Mining Promotion Corp to exploit a site in Dong Pao, a mineral-rich area some 400 km northwest of Hanoi.
Two of LG's subsidiaries, LG Metals and LG International, hold 40 percent and 20 percent stakes respectively with VNMC's Terraprodex, which has a 30 percent share.
The remaining 10 percent is held by Korea Mining Promotion Corp, the statement said.
Under the agreement, signed on Friday, LG Metals will provide the technologies required for extracting rare earth minerals from Dong Pao.

The extracted minerals will be refined into magnetic materials at LG Metals' rare earth magnet plant in Tianjin, China for use in the production of electronic appliances by LG Electronics, and other manufacturers in the global electronic appliance industry.

Construction of the mine would begin by the end of this year and production was expected to start in the middle of 1998. Annual revenues from the mine were expected to total about $8.0 million, the statement said.

"This partnership is only the first step in LG's development of rare earth mineral resources in Vietnam. Logically, our next step forward will be to look into the possibility of establishing manufacturing facilities for rare earth magnets here," said Gu-Myung Choi, president of LG Metals, who was present at the contract signing ceremony held in Vietnam.
